name: OPA350 / OPA2350 / OPA4350 (Burr-Brown CMOS rail-to-rail single-supply)
tagline: Burr-Brown 38 MHz rail-to-rail CMOS op-amp for 5 V rails. Japanese low-voltage CMoy builders say the OPA2350 sounds thick and 'BB-like', with solid bass.
technology: CMOS, rail-to-rail input and output (output within 10 mV of the rails), unity-gain stable, 2.7-5.5 V single supply, 38 MHz GBW, 22 V/us, 5 nV/rtHz (high-frequency spot figure)

part_numbers.status: unknown (TI product page is live; lifecycle not confirmed)
part_numbers.notes: Single. Comes in MSOP-8, SO-8 and DIP-8.
Dual. Comes in MSOP-8 (VSSOP), SO-8 and DIP-8. TI product page shows ACTIVE.

part_numbers.status: unknown (TI product page is live; lifecycle not confirmed)

lineage.notes: Designed as a Burr-Brown single-supply CMOS op-amp. Old mirrors use the Burr-Brown-style title 'High-Speed, Single-Supply, Rail-to-Rail OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIERS'.
TI datasheet SBOS099 is dated September 2000 and was last revised in December 2015 (rev D). The OPA2350 shows as ACTIVE.

key_specs.condition: typ; a high-frequency spot figure (believed f = 100 kHz, unconfirmed). CMOS 1/f noise likely makes the audio-band figure higher.

key_specs.value: -40 C to +85 C specified; -55 C to +150 C operating

key_specs.source: model memory; not confirmed in this check

reputation.summary: Praise for this family comes mainly from Japanese hobbyist writing. On nabe's blog (nabe.adiary.jp), in the op-amp spec/sound list and the low-voltage headphone-amp articles, the OPA2350 is said to sound thick (音に厚みがあり), with solid bass and a 'BB-like' character. The blog says it has more body than the AD822, works even without an output buffer, and is a recommended DIP choice for 5 V CMoy-style builds. It also comes up in a kakaku.com thread on small 3 V headphone amps. The OPA2353 praise cited here is for the sibling part, not the OPA2350. Western audiophile coverage is thin.
typical_uses: low-voltage portable headphone amps (per nabe, can run without an output buffer)
single-supply audio processing and ADC driving (TI's stated applications)
caveats: The absolute maximum supply is only about 5.5 V. Do not drop it into a +/-12 V or +/-15 V op-amp socket, where it will be destroyed.
The praise is subjective and comes from a few Japanese hobbyist sources.
The 5 nV/rtHz headline is a high-frequency figure. Being CMOS, noise in the audio band is likely higher.
Rail-to-rail input uses complementary input pairs, so behavior can change in the input crossover region. See the datasheet.
Quiescent current is relatively high for battery use (about 5 mA per amplifier, unconfirmed).

revision_history.changes: First SBOS099-numbered release at the time of the Burr-Brown/TI transition. Any earlier Burr-Brown document is not identified.

Current revision. Probably a conversion to TI's modern datasheet format (ESD ratings, pin-function tables, application/layout sections), but the change list was not confirmed. No die change is indicated.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports specific to this family were found. Take generic care with DIP-8 OPA2350PA bought from marketplace sellers. A remarked non-rail-to-rail part would show up as poor output swing near the rails at 5 V.
alternatives: OPA2353 (lower-power CMOS rail-to-rail sibling, also praised in Japanese CMoy builds)
AD822 (JFET-input single-supply dual; nabe's comparison point)
open_questions: Introduction year of the OPA350 family and any pre-September-2000 Burr-Brown datasheet (pre-SBOS numbering) were not found.
The date of SBOS099B and the change lists for revs A-D were not found. It is also unknown which mirror holds rev A (July 2001).
It is not established whether any TI RFAB fab-transfer or die-revision PCN covers OPA350/OPA2350/OPA4350. Such PCNs exist for other TI amplifiers (2021-2023), but none was linked to this family.
Lifecycle status of OPA350, OPA4350 and of the DIP OPA2350PA is not confirmed; only the OPA2350 base part was confirmed ACTIVE.
Check the frequency behind the 5 nV/rtHz figure (believed 100 kHz), the noise at 1 kHz, and quiescent current against SBOS099D.
